q1.context: Z is a pre-treatment baseline characteristic measured BEFORE the intervention T was assigned. Units with higher Z were more likely to receive T. Z plausibly affects the outcome Y directly.

q2.context: Z is measured AFTER the intervention T. Z is influenced by T AND by a separate unmeasured factor; that same unmeasured factor also affects the outcome Y. Z itself has no causal effect on Y.

q3.context: Z is measured AFTER the intervention T and is believed to lie ON the causal pathway from T to the outcome Y (T changes Z, and Z changes Y).
